strings.title: The Midnight Pharmacy
strings.hint: A theft whose loot is never sold is no theft. Who unlocked the door with a key, then broke the glass from inside?
strings.solvedText:
Culprit: nephew Sami Khalil — the sole heir.

Mounting debts and a stubborn uncle who refused to sell the pharmacy, his life's work. Sami entered at night with his key, strangled his uncle during stocktaking, then staged a robbery by drug users: he smashed the glass from inside, scattered medicines, and took narcotic medication to complete the story.

What convicted him: glass scattered outward rather than inward, the entire 'stolen' stock hidden in his car without being offered for sale, and an ATM camera recording his car near the pharmacy at 23:50 — an hour after he claimed to have gone to sleep.
strings.summary.text: In the old neighborhood, pharmacist Anwar Khalil, who had spent 40 years behind the same counter, was found strangled among his ransacked shelves. The storefront was smashed and the controlled-drug cabinet emptied. Everyone blamed a familiar drug user who lingered nearby. But the investigator lingered over the shattered glass: every fragment lay on the pavement... outside.
strings.summary.photoCap: Scattered storefront glass — direction of breakage
strings.summary.victim.name: Anwar Khalil
strings.summary.timeline[0].l: Closes the pharmacy and begins monthly stocktaking
strings.summary.timeline[1].l: A familiar car passes the ATM camera
strings.summary.timeline[3].l: Morning vendor discovers the broken storefront
strings.scene.intro: A robbery scene almost too perfect: theatrical disorder, open drawers with nothing valuable taken, and a back door unlocked without a scratch. The glass was broken outward from inside — after the crime, not before it.
strings.scene.photos[0].cap: Glass fragments on the pavement outside
strings.scene.notes[0]: Glass scattered outward — broken from inside
strings.scene.notes[1]: Back door opened with a key
strings.scene.notes[2]: Controlled-drug cabinet emptied with expert selectivity
strings.evidence[0].title: Direction of Glass Breakage
strings.evidence[0].desc: The fragment pattern is conclusive: the blow came from inside — a staged break-in.
strings.evidence[1].title: The Back Door
strings.evidence[1].desc: Opened with an original key. Copies belonged to the victim and his nephew; the dismissed representative had formally returned his.
strings.evidence[2].title: Narcotic Medication Packs
strings.evidence[2].desc: All the 'stolen goods' remained unopened and had never been offered on the black market.
strings.evidence[3].title: ATM Camera Image
strings.evidence[3].desc: Sami's car passes at 23:50, contradicting his claim that he had been asleep since ten.
strings.evidence[4].title: Draft Will
strings.evidence[4].desc: The uncle was changing his will: a large share to charity instead of 'someone undeserving.'
strings.evidence[5].title: The Known Drug User's File
strings.evidence[5].desc: A history of petty theft — but on the night of the crime, he was detained at a nearby police station after a fight!
strings.suspects[0].name: Dismissed representative Hatem
strings.suspects[0].relation: Dismissed by the victim for alleged misconduct
strings.suspects[0].alibi: 'I work nights as a delivery driver. The trip app records every minute.'
strings.suspects[0].statement: He fired me unfairly and ruined my reputation with the companies. I truly hated him. But I made eight documented trips that night. Hatred does not stop my meter running.
strings.suspects[1].name: Sami Khalil
strings.suspects[1].alibi: 'I went to sleep at ten. My neighbor heard my television.'
strings.suspects[1].statement: My uncle raised me after my father died, and I helped with stocktaking every month. Personal circumstances made me late that night, and the guilt will kill me. My car? ATM cameras make mistakes, and cars look alike. Besides, what would I do with medicines whose names I do not even know?
strings.suspects[2].name: Abu al-Rous, a drug user
strings.suspects[2].alibi: 'I was locked up after the cafe fight — ask the station itself!'
strings.suspects[2].statement: Every time glass breaks in this neighborhood, you name me. Uncle Anwar was the only one who gave me medicine on credit. I wish I had been there. Maybe I could have defended him.
strings.witnesses[0].name: Morning vendor
strings.witnesses[0].statement: The mess was strange: drawers overturned, but the cash box untouched. What thief leaves cash and takes boxes of medicine?
strings.witnesses[1].name: Building neighbor
strings.witnesses[1].statement: Around midnight, I heard a quiet conversation inside — two voices that knew each other, not shouting thieves.
strings.witnesses[2].name: Market guard
strings.witnesses[2].statement: The glass broke long after midnight. I passed at one, and the storefront was intact. Everything was quiet.
strings.folders[0].name: Incident reports
strings.folders[0].docs[0].title: Morning Report
strings.folders[0].docs[0].body: Report of a broken storefront and a body inside the pharmacy. Initial suspicion: robbery by drug users.
strings.folders[1].name: Forensic evidence
strings.folders[1].docs[0].title: Glass Examination Report
strings.folders[1].docs[0].body: 90% of the fragments were scattered outside. The glass was broken from inside after the death to stage the scene.
strings.folders[1].docs[1].title: Strangulation Report
strings.folders[1].docs[1].body: Manual strangulation from behind. The victim was seated doing stocktaking; the culprit stood behind him without arousing suspicion.
strings.folders[2].name: Interviews
strings.folders[2].docs[0].title: Representative Interview
strings.folders[2].docs[0].body: App records cover the entire night with consecutive trips. He is ruled out.
strings.folders[2].docs[1].title: Nephew Interview
strings.folders[2].docs[1].body: He denied passing through the market. Shown the ATM image, he said: 'Perhaps I went out for cigarettes and forgot.'
strings.folders[2].docs[2].title: Drug User Interview
strings.folders[2].docs[2].body: Detention records completely clear him: he was in a holding cell during the crime.
strings.folders[3].name: Records
strings.folders[3].docs[0].title: Sami's Debt Record
strings.folders[3].docs[0].body: Defaulted loans and a seizure notice, plus a broker's offer to buy the pharmacy property 'as soon as ownership is clear.'
strings.folders[3].docs[1].title: Key Copy Record
strings.folders[3].docs[1].body: An earlier official record confirms the representative returned his key. The remaining holders: the victim and his nephew.
strings.folders[4].name: Confidential files
strings.folders[4].docs[0].title: Car Search Record
strings.folders[4].docs[0].body: All the narcotic medication was in the car's rear storage compartment, still in the pharmacy's own bag. He did not even know how to 'sell' his stolen goods.
strings.folders[4].docs[1].title: The Unfinished Will
strings.folders[4].docs[1].body: The uncle's draft: 'As for the one waiting for my death to sell my walls, let him inherit the waiting.' He knew... and died at the hands of the person he had understood.
strings.reports[0].title: The Staged Scene Report
strings.reports[0].author: Scene examination team
strings.reports[0].body: Every element of the 'robbery' was added after the killing: glass broken the wrong way, selective disorder, and untouched money. A family crime staged to look like an outsider's.
strings.reports[1].title: Inheritance Report
strings.reports[1].author: Assigned investigator
strings.reports[1].body: The imminent amendment to the will would have deprived the sole heir of the property. The timing is no coincidence.
strings.notes[0].text: A thief who leaves the cash? Check the glass direction
strings.notes[1].text: Who can stand behind the pharmacist without making him turn?
